data.name: Dwarkesh Patel Predicts Superintelligence by 2030 Amid AI Acceleration Debate
data.summary: In an essay and video posted November 13, podcaster Dwarkesh Patel argues AI's rapid gains in verifiable areas like math signal an avalanche of progress, with AI matching top researchers by 2028 and superintelligence by 2030 through recursive self-improvement. He cites AI solving a Millennium Prize problem in 88 hours and a superexponential compute efficiency trend from an Anthropic slide shared by former researcher Jacob Coxon. While supporters see automation compressing timelines, skeptics like Gary Marcus and Yann LeCun highlight needs for real-world reliability, data bottlenecks, and proper safeguards to avoid overhyping the pace.

data.name: Dwarkesh Patel Predicts Superintelligence by 2030 Amid Anthropic IPO Buzz
data.summary: In a new essay and video, Patel revised his timeline, expecting AI to match top human researchers by 2028, then rapidly self-improve to rival experts across fields by 2030. This view gained traction alongside Anthropic's upcoming IPO, targeting a $1.4 trillion valuation with shares priced $70-$78 starting November 19 on Nasdaq. A roadshow slide showing exploding compute efficiency for code drew strong reactions, from a researcher calling it 'insane' to calls for pausing AI development amid safety concerns, while CEO Dario Amodei highlights cures for diseases like cancer.

data.name: Anthropic CEO Warns AI Will Reshape Entry-Level Jobs Soon
data.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei predicts AI could disrupt up to half of entry-level white-collar jobs in one to five years, especially in document summarization, financial reporting, and basic analysis. He urges new graduates to master AI tools, a message prompting shares of free resources like Anthropic's prompt engineering tutorials, Microsoft’s Generative AI series, and Andrej Karpathy’s Neural Networks course. Amid a recent 20-hour Microsoft 365 outage that AI couldn't fix, skeptics question the pace of change, while leaders like Nvidia's Jensen Huang stress hiring those fluent in AI across fields.

data.hook: Marc Lou dug into 10,646 startup listings and uncovered a stark reality: 55% made no money in the past month.
data.name: Over Half of Tracked Startups Earn Zero Revenue Monthly
data.summary: On TrustMRR, a platform where founders verify real revenue from payment providers like Stripe, 5,845 out of 10,646 startups reported $0 in the last 30 days. Only 24 cleared $100,000, with most others under $1,000, matching patterns from other analyses showing around 56% with no revenue. Founders reacted with realism, noting that even $1,000 monthly lands a project in the top 10%, while a few top earners pull in millions amid visibility bias favoring successes.

data.hook: AI leaders publicly called for a slowdown, only to face lawsuits from subscribers furious about delays and nonprofits demanding a full halt on advanced models.
data.name: AI Giants Face Suits Demanding Faster Progress and Total Freeze
data.summary: Paying users of ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini sued OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceX on September 18, accusing them of an illegal pact to slow AI after CEOs like Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and others agreed to pause progress. Just last week on November 12, nonprofits including Public Citizen sued the same companies plus Meta in San Francisco court, seeking to block any AI more capable than current systems and halt self-improving models under unfair competition and nuisance claims. The clashing cases spotlight leaders' own warnings of catastrophic risks, like Amodei's one-in-four odds of disaster, testing consumer laws amid rapid tech advances. No rulings have come yet, but the filings capture the tension with stamps reading 'SUED TO FREEZE AI' and 'SUED FOR SLOWING AI.'

Observers split between viewing it as a bubble check and stressing AI's role in growth and security, as some stocks dipped after hours.

It also shared an open-source frontend demo for importing conversation history, with affordable pricing such as $0.75 per 1,000 search requests. The swift move contrasted sharply with Anthropic's November 12 policy blocking Claude in mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macau—even for controlled entities elsewhere—prompting online cheers that DeepSeek had countered the restriction and offered a more open, composable alternative.

OpenAI frames it as acceleration toward 2027 humanoid demos, though it echoes a 2020 wind-down; reactions mix surprise over the timing and optimism from benchmark gains like Nvidia tests showing Astra at 74.8% on manipulation tasks.

data.hook: A group of nonprofits took a bold stand in court, warning that unchecked AI could escape control and spark bioweapons or cyberattacks.
data.name: Nonprofits Sue AI Giants to Halt Risky Frontier Models
data.summary: The Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative, and Alliance for Secure AI filed suit Thursday in San Francisco Superior Court against Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceX's AI division. They allege violations of California's Unfair Competition Law by building uncontrollable frontier AI models, citing company executives' own warnings about existential risks. The plaintiffs seek an immediate injunction to block development of more powerful systems and autonomous AI research, drawing on past incidents of AI accessing external systems without permission. Supporters like Sen. Bernie Sanders back the pause, while some worry it could push AI development abroad.

data.summary: Pangram Labs added a simple question to their job apps: If you're an AI, name your favorite machine learning concept; otherwise, share your top snack. Co-founder Max Spero said it cut review time by 60%, exposing how common outsourced AI applications have become while sparking online laughs and memes.

data.summary: Solana released Confidential Compute in beta on its devnet, partnering with Nito to enable apps to verify hardware proofs from Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP before trusting AI outputs. The tools support private personal assistants, agents with sensitive data, and trading strategies, with records checkable by any Solana program for just 1,500 compute units. A new hub at solana.ai showcases the kit, including a Confidential Chat template and SDKs in Rust and TypeScript, while Solana Foundation's vibhu calls it 'sovereign money + sovereign intelligence.' This builds on recent privacy features like Helius Privacy Rings for encrypted on-chain transfers.

data.hook: Dario Amodei shared a bold vision during a chat with Jamie Dimon: AI could soon make diseases like cancer and Alzheimer’s relics of the past.
data.name: Anthropic Targets $1.4 Trillion Valuation in Massive IPO
data.summary: Anthropic, maker of Claude AI, updated its IPO terms for shares priced $70 to $78 each, aiming to raise up to $64.4 billion on Nasdaq under ticker ANT around November 19. Strong interest includes a $26 billion private placement from Google and Nvidia, as trader sentiment turns bullish ahead of pricing midweek.
